utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, bon jour. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88/1-PT, the Prosecutor versus Milorad Trbic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Trbic, good morning, to you. I just want to make sure you are receiving interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And the Prosecution is Mr. Vanderpuye and Ms. Soljan, and for the Defence it's Mr. Piletta-Zanin assisted by --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [interpretation] Madam Elisa Krahenbuhl. The name in writing will be given to the court reporter later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is a special Status Conference that we have convened during which we will discuss -- we will give a resume of the latest developments in the case, which are in themselves the reasons for some concerns that we have that we will share with you and also hopefully, if he's prepared to discuss matters with us, later on in due course with the accused himself. We will stay in open session for a while, and then when we address ourselves to certain matters that require us to be in closed session, then we'll conduct the rest of the business in closed session. You will all recall that a few months ago on the 26th of June of this year the Trial Chamber, who was then -- which was then differently composed, ordered the severance of this case against Mr. Trbic, the case against Mr. Trbic from that of the other seven co-accused in the so-called Srebrenica 2 trial. It's Prosecution versus Popovic et al. Pretty soon after, and that's on the 14th of July, we issued a confidential decision granting the Defence a request for certification of the severance decision that I mentioned already. On the 20th of June, the duty judge issued a confidential order granting the Defence a request to suspend the time limits concerning these appeal proceedings until further order. The suspension remains in force. I'm referring to the duty judge in the Appeals Chamber, and that was Judge Schomburg, as you will recall. That decision to suspend the time limits is still valid. Before we had even decreed the severance of the case, the Office of the Prosecutor had filed a motion for the referral of Mr. Trbic under Rule 11 bis of our Rules to be tried in Bosnia and Herzegovina. That was on the 4th of May. Six days later, on the 10th of May, the matter was referred to -- this matter was referred to the Referral Bench by the President of this Tribunal, and on the latest development that we have is -- goes back to a couple of days ago, 22nd of November, 2006, when the Referral Bench issued an order for further submissions on the referral request and Scheduling Order for hearing. Basically, the Referral Bench notes that questions have been raised by the Pre-Trial Chamber seized of these proceedings, the pre-trial proceedings, relating to the mental health of the accused and that the Referral Bench wishes to obtain submissions from the parties and the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina on the provisions of Bosnian law, or the law of Bosnia and Herzegovina, addressing an accused's possible lack of fitness to enter a plea and to stand trial, and also on the compatibility of the legal system of Bosnia and Herzegovina with Rule 11 bis (B) under these conditions. I will stop here for a moment, because from our experience here, we usually note that while counsel for the accused to have received a copy of such an order, such a decision, relatively straight away upon -- or soon after filing, it's not usually the case with the accused who requires first to have the order or the decision translated into his own language. So first thing that we want to ensure ourselves of, make sure of, is whether Mr. Trbic has received or has been notified with -- served with a copy of this decision in his own language. Perhaps either you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, or Mr. Trbic, directly can -- I don't know if you -- I suppose you have discussed this with him already.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The accused is not aware of the decision for a very simple reason. I myself was travelling when the decision arrived on my desk. I saw Mr. Trbic very early yesterday morning, so I myself had not been aware of this decision when I saw him, and I did not have the time it took to have it translated. So he didn't see it in his language. A brief summary might, therefore, be useful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. This was the brief summary. I can, for your benefit, Mr. Trbic, read out slowly the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it's better, because we've got very limited time and we need to continue with the other case. I think you will certainly have an opportunity to try and explain to the -- to your client the decision of the Referral Bench. But basically it's what I noted just a few minutes ago, that the Referral Bench is moving, and it has highlighted to us and to you, and to you, of course, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that the mental health of your client is a real issue that needs to be addressed, and I'll come to that later on. Now, you will recall in particular -- particularly you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, and also Mr. Trbic, that during the Status Conference of the 15th of September, which -- over which I presided, and I think Ms. Soljan was here but not you, Mr. Vanderpuye, the accused chose to make some statements spontaneously. He stated that he did not have any problems at the Detention Unit. He also stated that his state of mental and physical health was stable and good, and that attempts to obtain medical expertise on this matter were unnecessary and unjustified. He also stated that he wished his case to be referred to the authorities of Bosnia and Herzegovina under the procedure of our Rule 11 bis, and that all other requests were unnecessary. He added that he had spoken to Mr. Piletta-Zanin about this for a long time and was aware that the referral matter was not yet decided but that it was still pending before the Referral Bench. He added that he did no longer stand by his previous statements and requested that these be ignored or no longer considered. And last but not least, he stated that he was not bothered by the issue of disclosure of his identity in the media and that he did not have any problems at the Detention Unit in relation to that. In the past months, on a regular basis we have been asked to continue authorising or advise the President about authorising, continuing to authorise the health of Mr. Trbic each time for a period of 30 days, and the last request has been -- goes back to a few days ago, rather almost a month, to the 31st of October, and that kind of monitoring order is still in force. I am now proceeding to give some details about matters relating to the issue of whether the accused is fit, medically fit, to enter a plea and to stand trial. You will recall that months ago we ourselves had asked the Registrar to appoint a psychiatrist to examine the accused. The Registrar appointed a psychologist first, who gave us -- came forward with a report which, for whatever it was worth, and it was worth everything that one could expect from a psychologist, we accept it, but the report itself indicated that the matter should be studied further, the accused should be examined further by a fully fledged professional psychiatrist. The Registrar appointed a psychiatrist. The psychiatrist examined the accused with what was available. He came out with an assessment which raised doubts as to the mental capacity of the accused to stand trial; however, also made it clear that this was not a time assessment. The assessment was based on the condition of the accused at the time and would be need -- would be needed -- would need to be reviewed from time to time until there was -- there came a stage when a final assessment could be reached. This was happening at a time when the Prosecution was not aware of the fact that it was happening, and it was then decided that there was no point in hiding this from the Prosecution any further. It was being done, of course --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I'm being advised by my colleagues that perhaps it would be better if we go into private session, and I have absolutely no objection to that. So we continue in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, I say it's a pity that you have decided not to cooperate with us, Mr. Trbic, in spite of our efforts to make you understand that this is in your own interest. I'm sure that when you are back in the Detention Unit, in your cell, you will have time to think about this. If you come to the conclusion -- if you change your mind, will you please let us know? And it will help us immensely.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will most certainly not change my mind. There is no need for that. Everything I have said holds true. That is indeed my opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank everyone. I thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, team members of the OTP team, and there will be a subsequent Status Conference in due course. I can't tell you exactly when, but within the [microphone not activated] of the Rules.
